A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MeGA, with readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting direct comparison. All 14 pages of v1 and 11 pages of v2 were inspected. Neither contains an appendix or embeds the separately referenced supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original NeRSemble experiments, including numerical comparisons in Table 1, component ablations in Table 2, and qualitative rendering and editing results.

after.justification: v2 reports original rendering comparisons, geometry-error measurements, component ablations and qualitative editing results in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–5.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds Gaussian smoothing of the binary occlusion mask before blending, replacing Ag times Mo with Ag times G(Mo). Equation 15 also drops the hair-silhouette penalty from the reported joint objective. These refine the retained mesh, neural-texture and Gaussian-hair framework.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NeRSemble head avatars through novel-view synthesis, novel-expression synthesis, hairstyle alteration and texture editing. The additional geometry metric and comparisons do not establish new datasets, populations or input scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 adds DELTA and Gaussian Head Avatar with super-resolution to the evaluated comparisons in Table 1 and Figure 4. PointAvatar and GaussianAvatars remain. This substantially broadens the comparator set beyond the two methods evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: v2 introduces geometry MAE between reconstructed and rasterized depth maps and a new 5,023-vertex no-subdivision control. The stated image resolution, camera/expression splits and rasterization-mask evaluation remain unchanged. Omission of PointAvatar configuration details does not establish a changed setting.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds mesh-subdivision and no-early-stopping ablations, with geometry errors and expanded visual evidence in Figure 5. v1's hard-pruning test and three explicit regularization-ablation rows are absent from the supplied v2. v2 refers loss-ablation details to unavailable supplementary material, substantially changing the inspectable analysis.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Averaging performance across subjects is retained.

E6.justification: v2 newly includes numerical novel-view comparisons and geometry errors. MeGA's reported novel-expression PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS changes from 32.47/0.947/0.058 to 32.59/0.949/0.057; its subject-306 ablation PSNR changes from 33.16 to 33.57. New comparator and ablation results appear, while per-subject comparison rows disappear. These are updated results alongside a method revision.

T1.justification: The blending-mask definition is mathematically revised to include Gaussian smoothing, and Equation 15 removes a loss term. These are substantive changes to the formal formulation, although the remaining mathematics is largely retained and neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the headline claims of a first hybrid mesh-Gaussian full-head representation, higher-quality novel-view and novel-expression rendering, and support for hairstyle alteration and texture editing. The expanded evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking eye/mouth interpenetration to Gaussian accumulation, blending instability to fluctuating depths, and Gaussian Head Avatar's expression-generalization weakness to implicit deformation and super-resolution. v1's specific explanation connecting diffuse-texture regularization to successful editing is omitted from the supplied v2.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release link and specifies that the per-pixel MLP has 307 learnable parameters. Conversely, v1's explicit PointAvatar limit of 240,000 points and 32GB V100 constraint are omitted, with baseline training details referred to supplementary material. The PDFs establish these documentation changes, not an actual change to that baseline configuration.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through an explicit comparison with DELTA's hybrid representation and additional Gaussian-avatar and anti-aliasing literature. However, Section 2.1 also newly groups references 46 and 47 with parametric head-avatar methods, although their bibliography titles concern fluid simulation and visual SLAM. Publication updates to existing references are not new works.

P1.justification: The abstract and many introduction, method and experiment paragraphs are extensively rewritten. Section 3.3 is reorganized around training stability and blending artifacts, and the ablation narrative is restructured. Acknowledgements and revised author information are added, while the main section sequence remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout with substantial figure rearrangement. Figure 2 adds the smoothing stage, Figures 4–5 expand their comparisons, Table 1 switches from per-subject results to method averages across two tasks, and Table 2 changes its controls and metric columns.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports the rendering and geometry claims through relevant additional baselines, explicit novel-view scores, geometry MAE and targeted ablations. The clearer blending explanation and code pointer also help. These gains are partly offset by losing per-subject results, explicit regularization-ablation scores and baseline configuration details from the supplied PDF, and by newly misplaced citations in Section 2. The net improvement is supported but limited.
